assessment: The ten is the deck's next half-step: extend the verified kill-web and feed the engines that already pass checkers. A 34-card bench was ranked and its top eight kept; two pool cards beat the bench tail — Marauding Blight-Priest (two new loop pairings, in-tribe) over spare bodies like Vampire Interloper, and Bloodchief Ascension (the index's one-mana hit on Sanguine Bond's shape) over Stensia Masquerade. Per strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors, 'consistency has two purchases: redundancy (more cards doing the job) or tutoring (cards that fetch it)' — this ten buys redundancy: a third lose-half for the 2x2 loop matrix, a second and third sac outlet, and the bench's only repeatable draw engine. Everything else in the box is depth behind a 29-body maindeck; the notable stay-offs carry verdict lines below.

combo_lines_opened.produces: Infinite lifegain triggers, infinite lifeloss, infinite lifegain
Infinite lifegain triggers, infinite lifeloss, infinite lifegain

ten.why: A third lose-half for the verified 2x2 kill-web: 'whenever you gain life, each opponent loses 1 life' pairs with both in-deck gain-halves, and it drains each opponent — no per-iteration retargeting like the Vito lines walk in stacks 001/004.
ten.unlocks: Two new pairings (with Exquisite Blood and with Bloodthirsty Conqueror) turn the verified 2x2 into a 2x3; as a Vampire it also banks an eminence token on cast and takes the Herald's Horn discount.

ten.why: Every Viscera Seer sacrifice, Grave Pact edict and table death is a counter; she dies into that many lifelink tokens, doubled through Anointed Procession and Mondrak, and each token entry is a separate Purphoros trigger by stack 008's per-entry counting.
ten.when: Sleeve once games show the Seer/Celebrant/Grave Pact web producing multiple deaths per turn cycle — she is the death engine's wrath-math payoff.

ten.why: One mana buys the drain shape the index lists as Sanguine Bond's lower-CMC hit; stack 003's 14-per-opponent attack turn charges all three quest counters in a single combat, after which every card hitting any opponent's graveyard drains 2 and gains 2.
ten.unlocks: A turn-1 play under the curve that taxes wraths, draw-steps and fetches for the rest of the game — the cheapest new drain engine the pool offers, and the best-ranked candidate anywhere in this analysis (EDHREC 742).

ten.why: Draw is the role budget's biggest hole (7 short); Purifier converts the lifegain the deck produces every turn — lifelink bodies, Sanctum Seeker triggers, Cruel Celebrant deaths — into a card each end step for {2}.
ten.when: Sleeve when games stall on an empty hand by turn 6-7; it is the only repeatable draw engine on the bench.

ten.why: The maindeck holds exactly one sac outlet (Viscera Seer) feeding Grave Pact and Cruel Celebrant; a second one-mana outlet whose activation puts a counter on every Vampire keeps the edict engine alive through spot removal.
ten.when: Sleeve once Viscera Seer starts eating the table's first removal spell — outlet redundancy is the purchase.

ten.why: A third sac outlet that ramps: tap and sacrifice a spare token for {B}{B}{B} of Vampire/Cleric/Demon mana — a Grave Pact edict and a turn-4 five-drop from the same activation, in a deck 5 slots short on ramp.
ten.when: Sleeve alongside or instead of Indulgent Aristocrat when pod speed makes the mana burst matter more than tribe-wide counters.

ten.why: buff:attached is a named role gap, and on a Vampire the Blade grows +2/+2 per creature death — every Seer sacrifice, every Grave Pact edict, every board the table sweeps; on Edgar it makes commander damage a real clock.
ten.when: Sleeve for grindy pods where boards trade often; it is the cheapest permanent that monetizes the death web without attacking first.

ten.why: +2/+1 and flying to the whole tribe turns stack 003's seven-attacker, 14-per-opponent turn evasive — and Viscera Seer's free scry sets a black card on top on demand.
ten.when: Sleeve when the alpha strike is the primary kill at your pods and the loop halves are drawing the table's removal instead.

ten.card: Sorin of House Markov // Sorin, Ravenous Neonate
ten.type_line: Legendary Creature — Human Noble // Legendary Planeswalker — Sorin
ten.why: A two-mana lifelink extort body that flips to a planeswalker any turn you gained 3 or more life — near-automatic when one Sanctum Seeker attack with seven Vampires gains 7 — and extort turns every cheap Vampire spell into a table drain.
ten.when: Sleeve for grindier pods where a drain-per-cast rider and the flipped walker outvalue a fourth interchangeable two-drop body.

ten.why: The strategic frame's named tension is a single one-drop deathtouch defender (Vampire of the Dire Moon); Aetherborn adds a two-mana deathtouch-lifelink wall that trades up against anything and feeds every lifegain trigger while blocking.
ten.when: Sleeve against aggressive pods — the recall for the thin deathtouch web, and the cheapest body that defends without leaving the drain plan.

bench_verdicts.card: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose
bench_verdicts.why: The box copy duplicates a card already sleeved in the 99 — a spare, not a candidate.
Also a duplicate of a maindeck card; a spare, not a candidate.

bench_verdicts.card: Runo Stromkirk // Krothuss, Lord of the Deep
bench_verdicts.why: Outside Edgar's colour identity — unplayable in this deck.
The same deathtouch-lifelink job as Gifted Aetherborn for one more mana; the recall slot goes to the cheaper body.
One-shot modal value; the 7-card draw hole wants engines, not a single trigger.
An attack-gated draw engine that competes with Viscera Seer and Grave Pact for the same bodies, at combat speed only.

bench_verdicts.card: Aclazotz, Deepest Betrayal // Temple of the Dead
bench_verdicts.why: A strong five-drop in a curve that peaks at 2-3; its discard engine advances nothing the verified kills need.
Seven mana for haste and evasion the alpha strike would enjoy — but the deck's verified kills do not need combat to end the game.
A metagame card: sleeve it against graveyard pods, not by default.
Blood tokens without discard payoffs; its only bench partner (Wedding Security) is also off-list.
A Blood payoff in a 99 with almost no Blood producers.
A fourth lord at three mana behind Legion Lieutenant, Stromkirk Captain and Captivating Vampire — the pump axis is covered.

gaps: Marauding Blight-Priest's two lines and the frame's Cruel Celebrant ignition path are unverified — /resolve-stack scenarios would settle whether the new pairings resolve exactly as stacks 001/004/005/006 did.

Bloodchief Ascension's index hit is CMC-based; oracle text requires three quest counters before it drains, so 'upgrade over Sanguine Bond' is bounded to the index's own criteria, not an in-play dominance claim.
No EDHREC rank exists for any bench card, so the bench ranking rests on deck need alone.
The strategy corpus has no aristocrats or typal-lord section; outlet-redundancy and lord-density rankings here rest on oracle text and the role budget, not citable doctrine.
